messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and safely: | Step | What to Do | Tips & Best Practices | |------|------------|-----------------------| | **1. Research the Market** | • Look up recent sales of the same make/model on sites like Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local music‑store listings.
• Note the price range, condition, and any extras (case, strap, tuner). | • Use the “Sold” filter on Reverb to see actual sale prices, not just asking prices.
• Check the “Used” section on the manufacturer’s site for MSRP and typical resale values. | | **2. Clean & Prepare the Guitar** | • Wipe down the body, neck, and fretboard with a microfiber cloth.
• Remove dust from the soundhole and inside the body.
• Inspect for cracks, loose screws, or other damage. | • If you’re unsure about repairs, consider a quick tune‑up at a local shop; it can boost resale value. | | **3. Take High‑Quality Photos** | • Capture the front, back, side, headstock, soundhole, and any visible wear.
• Include a reference object (e.g., a ruler or a coin) for scale.
• Use natural light and a neutral background. | • A photo of the guitar in a case or on a stand can show it’s ready for transport. | | **4. Write a Clear, Honest Description** | • Include brand, model, year, wood type, finish, and any modifications.
• Mention the tuning, playability, and overall condition.
• List extras (case, strap, tuner, cleaning kit). | • Highlight unique features (e.g., custom inlay, limited edition).
• Avoid exaggeration; buyers appreciate transparency. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Reverb** – Great for musicians; offers shipping labels and buyer protection.
• **eBay** – Broad audience; auction or fixed‑price options.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – Local, no shipping needed.
• **Local Music Stores** – Consignment or direct sale; they’ll handle marketing. | • For local sales, use Facebook Marketplace or Craigslist for quick transactions.
• For national reach, Reverb or eBay are best. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | • Base your price on recent sales, condition, and extras.
• Consider adding a small buffer for negotiation (e.g., $50–$100 above your target). | • If you’re in a hurry, price slightly lower than the average to attract buyers quickly. | | **7. List Your Guitar** | • Upload photos, enter description, set price, and choose shipping options.
• On Reverb, you can opt for “Consignment” if you don’t want to ship yourself. | • Enable “Buy Now” if you want a quick sale; otherwise, allow offers. | | **8. Handle Inquiries Promptly** | • Respond within 24 hrs to keep buyers engaged.
• Be prepared to answer questions about tuning, playability, and shipping. | • Offer to send a video of the guitar playing if requested. | | **9. Arrange Payment & Shipping** | • For local sales: meet in a public place, accept cash or Venmo.
• For online sales: use Reverb’s integrated payment system or PayPal.
• Ship with a reputable carrier (USPS, UPS, FedEx) and insure the package. | • Reverb’s “Shipping Label” service includes insurance and tracking. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | • Once payment is confirmed, ship the guitar promptly.
• Keep the buyer updated with tracking info.
• Ask for a review on Reverb or eBay to build credibility. | • If you’re selling through a store, they’ll handle the transaction and may offer a commission. | ### Quick Checklist - [ ] Clean guitar & inspect condition - [ ] Take 5–7 high‑quality photos - [ ] Write honest, detailed description - [ ] Research recent sales & set price - [ ] List on Reverb, eBay, and/or local classifieds - [ ] Respond to inquiries within 24 hrs - [ ] Arrange safe payment & shipping - [ ] Ship promptly & track delivery ### Safety Tips - **Meet in a public place** (coffee shop, library, police station) for local sales. - **Bring a friend** or let someone know where you’re going. - **Accept secure payment** (PayPal, Venmo, or cash). - **Avoid wire transfers** or unverified payment methods. ### Optional Extras - **Reverb Consignment** – The store handles marketing, shipping, and takes a commission. - **Trade‑in Programs** – Some stores will buy your guitar outright or offer store credit. - **Local Music Shops** – Many accept used instruments for resale or consignment. By following these steps, you’ll maximize your chances of getting a fair price while keeping the process smooth and secure. Good luck with your sale!
